subject: maths
title: Place value and our number system

scenes.heading: Place value and our number system
scenes.sub: How just ten digits can write any number
scenes.say: With only ten digits, zero to nine, you can write the price of a phone or the crowd at the footy. The secret is place value: where a digit sits tells you what it's worth.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A row of boxes, each worth 10 times the box to its right
scenes.science: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right
scenes.breaks: A real box can hold any number of counters. A place can only hold 0 to 9 — at ten you swap for 1 in the next place.
scenes.say: Picture a row of boxes. The right box is worth one per counter, the next is worth ten, then a hundred, then a thousand. Moving one box left makes each counter worth ten times as much. But a place can only hold zero to nine. When you reach ten, you swap them for one counter in the next box.

scenes.heading: Place and value
points: Zero is a placeholder: 207 is not 27
scenes.say: A digit's value is the digit times its place. In five million, three hundred and forty thousand, eight hundred and twenty-seven, the four is worth forty thousand. The same digit can be worth different amounts, like the three fives in five hundred and fifty-five. And zero holds an empty place open, so two hundred and seven is not twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: A digit's value is the digit times its place. In 5 340 827, the 4 is worth 40 000. The same digit can be worth different amounts, like the three 5s in 555. And zero holds an empty place open, so 207 is not 27.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Write "twenty-three thousand and sixty" in numerals.
scenes.say: Write twenty-three thousand and sixty in numerals. The thousands group is twenty-three. The last group is sixty, written as zero six zero, because the zero holds the hundreds place. Put them together: twenty-three thousand and sixty. Check by adding the parts back up.
scenes.caption: Write "twenty-three thousand and sixty" in numerals. The thousands group is 23. The last group is sixty, written 060, because the zero holds the hundreds place. Together: 23 060. Check by adding the parts back up.

scenes.heading: Comparing whole numbers
steps: Count the digits: more digits is bigger
Same length? Start from the left
scenes.say: To compare whole numbers, first count the digits. More digits means bigger. If they have the same number of digits, compare from the left. The first column where the digits differ decides which is bigger.

scenes.heading: Digit vs value
scenes.say: Don't mix up a digit and its value. The digit is just the symbol you see. Its value depends on its column. In three million, seven hundred and forty-two thousand, six hundred and fifteen, the digit is seven, but its value is seven hundred thousand.
scenes.caption: Don't mix up a digit and its value. The digit is just the symbol you see. Its value depends on its column. In 3 742 615 the digit is 7, but its value is 700 000.

points: Each place is 10 × the one on its right
scenes.say: Quick recap. We use ten digits in a base-ten system. Each place is worth ten times the place to its right. Value equals digit times place. Zero keeps empty places open. And compare numbers from the left. Now try the practice questions!
